annotations.title: Get a one-click link to add a DMARC record

description: Get a link that adds a DMARC record (`v=DMARC1; p=none`, which only reports and blocks nothing) for this mailbox's sending domain at your DNS provider in one click, when the provider supports it. We offer it only when no DMARC record covers the domain and the domain's own `_dmarc` name holds no DMARC text, read from DNS when you ask, so a record you already have is never doubled. Open `url` in a browser: the provider asks you to sign in, shows the record and adds it once you approve, then sends you back to the console at `returnTo` (a console path like `/acme/mailboxes`; left out, the console's front page). Nothing changes until the person who runs the DNS approves. Coming back proves nothing, so call check_mailbox_domain to read the record. When `url` is null, `reason` says why: `not_set_up` (this server can't sign links, so the feature is off), `not_offered` (the DNS provider can't add our record in one click, the domain is a reserved name like acme.test, or the domain's `_dmarc` name already holds a DMARC record that receivers ignore: replace it by hand with the DMARC row in check_mailbox_domain's `domainAuth.records`), `unanswered` (DNS or the provider didn't answer in time: retry before changing DNS) or `nothing_to_add` (a DMARC record already covers the domain). With a link, `provider` names the DNS provider. The link is offered only at DNS providers that accepted our template. At most 30 a minute per workspace.

returnTo.description: A console path, with its query if it has one, where the DNS provider sends the person back after they approve the record, like /acme/settings. Not a full address, and no # part. Left out, they land on the console's front page.
